must_fix.what: Ctrl-C does not stop a run, and a second Ctrl-C leaves the tests running with no time limit. The worker threads are not daemon threads and each child has its own session. So the first SIGINT only raises KeyboardInterrupt in main's join(); the threads keep starting every pending unit until the list is empty, and then the run exits rc -2 with no tier<N>.json, no table and no last line. For tier 2 that is up to about 20 minutes of work that is then thrown away. A second SIGINT ends run_tiers at once, but the children it was running keep going after their time limit (the parent enforced the limit), and their per-unit HOME and TMPDIR folders (/tmp/graphite-tier-*) are never removed.
must_fix.where: tools/run_tiers.py run_all() (threads, lines 420-424) and run_unit() (the timeout lives only in the parent's child.wait)
must_fix.how_to_reproduce: Make a fake tree: tools/run_tiers.py, tools/check_hatch.py, a tools/tiers.json whose '0' lists test_sleep and test_sleep2, timeout_seconds module 6, and two tests_integrated modules that each time.sleep(90) inside a test. Start 'python tools/run_tiers.py 0 --out X' with SIGINT at its default handler (a non-interactive '&' job ignores SIGINT, so use Popen with preexec_fn resetting SIGINT). (a) Send one SIGINT after 2 s: the run goes on until both units reach their limit, then exits rc -2, and X holds only logs/ (no tier0.json). (b) Send two SIGINTs 0.5 s apart: run_tiers exits at once (traceback in threading._shutdown), and both test processes are still alive 10 s after their 6 s limit. On the real tier 0, one SIGINT at 8 s left it running 10 s later with 4 child processes. Each double interrupt also left two /tmp/graphite-tier-* folders behind. Fix: catch KeyboardInterrupt (or install a SIGINT/SIGTERM handler), stop handing out units, killpg every running child, remove its scratch folder, write the partial result with the interrupted units marked, exit non-zero. Add a test that interrupts a run of a sleeping fake module.

must_fix.what: Tier 1 misses the tests a staged rename breaks. changed_files() calls 'git diff --name-only --relative REF --'. Porcelain git diff detects renames by default, so after 'git mv workbench/old.py workbench/new.py' only workbench/new.py is listed. A test that imports workbench.old, which is now broken, is not chosen, and tier 1 passes. Moving or renaming a module is the change most likely to break its importers.
must_fix.how_to_reproduce: In a temporary git repo with workbench/old.py and tests_integrated/test_old.py ('from workbench import old'), commit, then 'git mv workbench/old.py workbench/new.py'. 'git diff --name-only --relative HEAD --' prints only workbench/new.py; with --no-renames it prints both names. Fix: add '--no-renames' to the diff call, and add a git mv case to test_the_changed_files_are_what_differs_from_the_commit_and_what_git_does_not_know.

should_fix: Skipped tests are not recorded. A module that skips all its tests is PASSED (a fake module with two @skip tests reads 'ran 2 failed 0 PASSED'), and tier 2 still prints '0 failing'. In the scene, Blocked counts as failing, so this is inconsistent: test_exact_math_solvers without SymPy or Z3, or test_startup_scripts' privilege skips, pass silently in the release tier. parse_unittest already returns 'skipped'; keep it in each row, show it in the table, and say it on the last line.

The crash branch in read_result ("if (rc or summary['verdict'] != 'OK') and not failed") has no test. With it replaced by 'if False', all 12 tests still pass, and a module that dies mid-test with exit 0 (os._exit) or crashes would read as PASSED. Add a fake module that calls os._exit(0) inside a test. With the branch in place, a fake os._exit(0) module and a real segfault (ctypes.string_at(0)) are both reported as failing.

read_result for the check, scene, integrity and sweep kinds has no test: a window check with no JSON or a non-PASSED state, a scene with fewer rows than cases or a Blocked row, a check_release crash with a stale release_check.json. Each is one fake script on the tree TheRunner already builds.

In the process-group fallback (the owner's ThinkPad as a normal user, where 'unshare --pid' is refused), the group is killed only at the time limit. A grandchild a module starts outlives the module after a normal exit. Checked: a fake test that Popen's 'sleep 23.5' and returns leaves the sleeper alive in fallback mode and none in namespace mode. Add os.killpg(child.pid, SIGKILL) after a normal exit too. docs/CHECKS.md line 24 ('so nothing it starts outlives it; elsewhere in a process group of its own') currently claims more than the fallback does.

DROPPED removes ARC1_WORKBENCH_CONFIG_HOME but not ARC_LEDGER_WORKSPACE. shell2.relaunch() sets that variable for every process the app starts after a workspace switch, and the deployment service script sets it too. locations.default_root() and doctor.chosen_root() obey it before anything else. ARC_LEDGER_EDITION, ARC_LEDGER_OPEN, ARC_LEDGER_FULLSCREEN, ARC_LEDGER_EMBEDDED, ARC_LEDGER_SUPERVISION and LEDGER_QUALIFICATION_SECRET also pass through. I ran tier 0 and all 22 window checks with ARC_LEDGER_WORKSPACE pointing at an empty sentinel folder, and nothing was written there, so no leak is shown today. A runner whose point is isolation should still drop them, the same as check_hatch should.

For the Graphite look the child gets GRAPHITE_APPEARANCE=graphite. The house rule's default look is the variable unset, where the session file decides (boss_theme.chosen_appearance). So no tier ever runs the true default path. Pop the variable for 'graphite' instead of setting it, or say in docs/CHECKS.md that the two are not the same.

The --out guard uses .absolute(), not .resolve(), and compares lexical parents. '/x/other/../<program>/zz', or a symlink that points into the program folder, passes the check, and the run then writes into the program. Resolve out and ROOT before comparing.

import_map recovers from a cache that is not JSON but crashes on JSON of the wrong shape: {"format":1,"files":[]} or {"format":1,"files":"x"} gives AttributeError ('list' object has no attribute 'get'). Tier 1 then fails until someone deletes ~/.cache/graphite-tiers/<hash>.json. Check that 'files' is a dict.

If run_unit raises in a worker thread (for example, the logs under --out cannot be written on a full disk, or an unexpected report shape), that thread dies with only a stderr traceback, its row stays None, and main() then crashes with TypeError in failing(). No result file is written and the failure is not named. Catch the exception per unit and record it as a failed row.

A changed file that is not Python is matched by a bare file-name substring. 'CHECKS.md' matches every file that says 'WINDOW_CHECKS.md', and 'README.md' matches about 20 modules. For this patch's own diff, tier 1 chose 30 units, 46 runs with tier 0. This is safe but makes tier 1 big for a doc edit. Match the relative path, or the name on a word boundary.

check_hatch.parse_unittest takes the first 'Ran N tests' line in stderr. A module that writes a nested unittest summary to stderr reports the wrong count (a fake reported 'ran 99'). Its failure was still caught. Use the last match in run_tiers, or fix it in check_hatch.
Tier 1 needs a git checkout even without --changed, because changed_files('HEAD') exits with a message. The installed kit is not a checkout. docs/CHECKS.md should say so.

summary: The tiered runner works as reported for normal runs. All new and touched modules pass in both looks. Tier 0 reproduced at 34 s with 0 failing, and the 22 window checks pass through the runner in 180 s. The builder's tier 2 and tier 1 numbers match their result files. Three of the four mutations were caught by the new tests. Two real defects need fixing before merge. (1) Interrupting a run does not work: the first Ctrl-C is ignored until every unit has run and then the results are thrown away; a second Ctrl-C leaves the running tests alive past their time limit and their temporary home folders behind. (2) Tier 1 uses git diff with rename detection on, so a staged rename hides the old name, and the tests it breaks are not chosen. The should-fix list is smaller. Skipped tests are invisible in '0 failing'. The crash branch and the non-module result readers have no tests. The process-group fallback, which the owner's machine will use, leaves grandchildren after a normal exit. ARC_LEDGER_WORKSPACE and related variables are not dropped (no leak shown). The Graphite look sets GRAPHITE_APPEARANCE instead of leaving it unset. The --out guard is lexical. A wrong-shape cache crashes tier 1. A worker exception crashes the run with no result file.
